message.reasoning_content:
Key claim: tie-break — bitonic sort with strict `>` comparison. Bitonic sort with cond (left > right) != flip — is it stable? Bitonic sort is not stable generally. Contract: ties must keep LOWER index. With strict > comparison and no index-based tie-break, when equal values, cond is false regardless... cond = (left > right) != flip. With equal values, left>right false, so cond = flip. For flip==1 (want swap to put larger first?), swapping happens. So ties may be reordered arbitrarily → lower index may not be kept. Test with tie-heavy inputs.

Record claim in_scope, then probe.
